    AI Overview
    Ratified in 1967, the 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution clarifies presidential succession and disability procedures
    . It establishes that the Vice President becomes President if the President dies, resigns, or is removed, and allows for the temporary transfer of power if the President is unable to discharge their duties. 
    Key Sections of the 25th Amendment: 
    • Section 1 (Succession): Explicitly states that if the President is removed, dies, or resigns, the Vice President becomes President.
    • Section 2 (Vice Presidential Vacancy): Allows the President to nominate a new Vice President if the seat is vacant, subject to a majority vote in both Houses of Congress
      .
    • Section 3 (Voluntary Transfer of Power): Enables the President to declare in writing they are unable to perform their duties, making the Vice President the Acting President until a written declaration to the contrary is submitted.
    • Section 4 (Involuntary Transfer of Power): Allows the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to declare the President disabled, immediately making the Vice President the Acting President. If the President contests this, Congress determines the outcome. 
    The amendment was adopted following the assassination of President John F. Kennedy to ensure continuity in the executive branch. While Section 3 has been used multiple times (often during medical procedures), Section 4 has never been invoked.
